subject: Finova SLOs & regional routing — post-demo next steps
messages:
---- MESSAGE 1 ----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@finova.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finova SLOs & regional routing — post-demo next steps

Hi Natalie / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. As discussed, I wanted to capture the performance targets and next steps so we can loop Engineering/SRE in and scope a short pilot. Attached is a draft SLO matrix (Finova_SLO_matrix_v2.xlsx) that maps the targets we spoke about to Redwood features/controls.

High-level asks from your side that I captured:
- Latency targets (p95) by region: US, EU, APAC (please confirm numbers below)
- Expected sustained throughput (req/s) and concurrency requirements
- Whether streaming responses are required for any flows (assistant/chat vs. batch generation)
- Any data residency/regulatory constraints (EU data staying in-region, logs retention, etc.)

What I have captured so far (please confirm or correct):
- US: p95 <= 100ms for single-turn generate calls (assistant mode may be higher)
- EU: p95 <= 120ms (data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU)
- APAC: p95 <= 200-250ms (APAC user base is latency sensitive, but some allowance expected)
- Throughput: ~1,200-1,500 req/s across peaks
- Peak concurrency: ~200 concurrent sessions (assistant flows hold connections for streaming)
- Streaming: required for live assistant; non-streaming ok for async batch jobs

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm the numbers above (reply with final targets)?
2) Once confirmed, I will put Aditya (SRE) and Rishi (solutions/infra) on copy to validate feasibility and propose architecture (regional endpoints, dedicated pools, caching).
3) Share a short list of sample calls/expected token sizes so we can estimate per-token latency and cost for the pilot.

I attached a regional_latency_map and a short draft MOP with rollout suggestions (redwood-draft-mop.docx). If the numbers above look right, can we schedule a 30-min architecture sync this week?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0124

---- MESSAGE 2 ----
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@finova.com>

Cc: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova SLOs & regional routing — post-demo next steps

Marissa — thanks for the write-up and the clear next steps. Numbers below are close to what we need; a few clarifications:

Confirmed targets (please use these):
- US: p95 <= 100ms for short assistant turns (under 128 tokens). p50 target of 45ms would be great but p95 is the critical SLA.
- EU: p95 <= 120ms, and importantly EU-origin data (requests + logs) must remain in EU for EU customers.
- APAC: p95 <= 220ms for Tokyo/Sydney users; if routing from a west-coast US region for some failover that's OK but we prefer regional endpoints in APAC for sustained load.
- Throughput: baseline 800 req/s, spike to 1,500 req/s for marketing events.
- Concurrency: sustained 150 concurrent assistant sessions, spiking to ~250 during promos.
- Streaming: required for the assistant flow (low-latency partial token delivery). For background batch generation (reports) streaming not required.

Other constraints:
- Data retention: audit logs retained for 13 months (SOC2/is a requirement for us)
- Encryption: keys managed by us via our KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we need to understand key control and auditability.

We can share sample payloads (assistant turn average ~80 tokens, long-turns 300 tokens, report jobs 2-5k tokens). I'll upload a small sample corpus to the Drive link you shared.

Let's do the architecture sync on Wed 10/07 at 09:00 PT if that works for your team and SREs.

Best,
Natalie
Head of Platform | Finova
Natalie.Chen@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova SLOs & regional routing — post-demo next steps

Thanks Natalie — that's very helpful and aligns with what I expected.

Aditya / Rishi — looping you both in to confirm feasibility and propose options. Key asks from Finova (confirmed):
- p95 targets by region as Natalie listed (US 100ms, EU 120ms, APAC 220ms)
- throughput baseline 800 req/s, spiking to 1,500 req/s across regions
- concurrency sustained 150, spikes to 250 for assistant streaming flows
- streaming mandatory for assistant; batch jobs are non-streaming
- EU data residency and 13-month audit log retention; Finova prefers customer-managed KMS for Private deployment, but we should propose hosted options with envelope encryption and audit hooks as an interim.

Attachments: I included the updated SLO matrix and regional latency map.

Suggested approach from Sales side: run a 4-week pilot with a dedicated pool in each target region (US/EU/APAC), start with a canary routing policy to 10% traffic, validate p95 under synthetic and real traffic, then bump to 50% and full cutover. For the pilot we can provide test keys and limited production traffic.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's prefix/KV caching + streaming optimization will help reduce p95 for assistant flows (we expect repeated context for sessions)? Also, what are the implications on cost if we keep dedicated pools in APAC vs using cross-region fallback?

I'll schedule Wed 10/07 09:00 PT for a 30-min sync and send calendar invites shortly.

--
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---- MESSAGE 4 ----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Natalie Chen <natalie@finova.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova SLOs & regional routing — post-demo next steps

Natalie / Alex / Marissa — quick engineering take ahead of Wed's sync. High level: all targets look achievable, but we should align on configuration and trade-offs.

Feasibility notes:
- Latency: p95 <= 100ms in US and 120ms EU for short turns (~<128 tokens) is reasonable with dedicated GPU pools in-region plus streaming enabled and KV/prefix caching. For APAC, to get to ~220ms we recommend at least one dedicated APAC pool (Tokyo or Sydney) — cross-region fallback from US west will generally add 80-150ms overhead which would make p95 inconsistent.
- Throughput & concurrency: 1,500 req/s peak with spikes to 250 concurrent streaming sessions is feasible if we size dedicated pools with autoscale and reserve burst capacity. We'll propose node counts in the architecture doc. Continuous batching and non-blocking streaming paths in our runtime will keep per-token latency low.
- Streaming: Redwood's streaming path avoids full-token blocking; however streaming does increase resource usage per session (long-lived connections). We need to size for connection concurrency separately from CPU/GPU throughput.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache will give large tail improvements for assistant flows with repeated prompts. We'll quantify expected p95 improvement after we see the sample corpus.
- Data residency / KMS: For EU residency we can deploy Private (VPC) in customer-managed region with local KMS integration to meet the customer's requirement. For hosted, we support envelope encryption and customer-provided KMS with audit logs, but some customers prefer Private for strict residency/controls.
- Cost trade-offs: Dedicated APAC pools increase committed cost; cross-region fallback reduces cost but makes p95 variable. We will include a cost/runway table in the architecture write-up.

Requested inputs before Wed:
1) Sample payload zip and representative token sizes (Natalie indicated you'll upload to Drive).
2) Any compliance docs (SOC2 scope) or additional retention constraints.
3) Which APAC region you prefer (Tokyo/Sydney) for the initial pilot.

Next steps (proposed):
- Wed 10/07 09:00 PT: 30-min architecture sync (Marissa to send invite)
- After sync: Redwood will produce an architecture + sizing doc (1-2 pages) and a pilot plan (week-by-week with success criteria).
- Provide pilot keys and test endpoints for Finova to run their load/testing in week 1.

I'll draft the architecture doc after the call and include node sizing options and cost delta for dedicated APAC vs fallback.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.inference
